import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Landing WI-37593 — whose entire subject was *"this guard is wired to nothing"* — my own fix
reproduced the bug it was fixing. Four traps, each of which independently produces a
**green that means "it stopped checking."**

## 1. A registration is skipped SILENTLY when the host workspace lacks the script

`scripts/affected-tests.mjs` appends a registered guard with:

```js
for (const guard of REPO_WIDE_INVARIANT_GUARDS) {
  const ws = wsByName.get(guard.workspace);
  if (!ws?.scripts?.[guard.script]) continue;   // <- silent skip
```

`guard.workspace` is normally `@papercusp/operator-core`. A guard whose npm script is
declared only in the **root** `package.json` therefore matches nothing and runs on **no
path at all**. The entry looks right, reads right, and reviews clean.

**Fix:** declare it in the host workspace too. The root scripts resolve `ROOT` from
`import.meta.url`, so cwd is irrelevant:

```json
"lint:workspace-deps-complete": "node ../../scripts/check-workspace-deps-complete.mjs"
```

## 2. `--print-affected` now reports guards too

The print-only probe now emits the original machine-readable workspace lines and a line for
each repo-wide guard task attached by the same selection:

```text
AFFECTED_WS	@papercusp/web
AFFECTED_GUARD	@papercusp/operator-core	lint:chunk-safe
```

Unlike the old behavior, guard selection happens before the probe exits. Guard lines can
therefore appear even when there are zero `AFFECTED_WS` lines, which is the intended
fail-safe behavior for root-level changes such as `package.json`.

The repo's own detector names inert registrations outright — **run this after any
registration**:

```bash
npm run lint:guard-reachability
# ❌ 1 REPO_WIDE_INVARIANT_GUARDS registration(s) are INERT — the workspace declares no such script
```

## 3. "Nothing invokes it" is usually wrong — check CI before you claim it

WI-37593 asserted the guard was invoked by nothing, evidenced by a grep of
`affected-tests.mjs`. That grep was correct and the conclusion was still too strong:
`.github/workflows/test.yml` runs it, so `lint:guard-reachability` classifies it
**`[ci]` = enforced**.

The accurate, narrower finding is the one worth carrying: git-sync stamps every commit
`[skip ci]`, so the `push`/`pull_request` triggers never fire
(EI-18661485259809120), and green-checkpoint dispatches the workflow only **after** it
fast-forwards `main`. Enforcement is therefore **remote and post-promotion** — the author
gets zero local signal and the fleet's blocking verdict never runs it. That is a real gap,
and registering in `REPO_WIDE_INVARIANT_GUARDS` is what closes it.

<Aside type="caution">
`--census` prints only the PROBLEM categories (not-enforced / partially-covered /
not-measured), never the enforced majority. A guard's absence from it means "classified
enforced", **not** "unknown" — and not "the local path is covered". It also writes via
`console.error`, so `cmd --census 2>&1 > f` sends the report to your terminal and leaves
you grepping an empty file. Use `> f 2>&1`.
</Aside>

## 4. A whole-file scanner eventually flags its own `selfTest()` fixtures

`hook-repo-root-portability.test.ts` (the "no guard script hardcodes its repo root"
ratchet) went red on `posttooluse-css-design-primitives-nudge.mjs` for `root = /repo`.
That binding is inside `function selfTest()` — a synthetic tree handed to a pure helper,
`isCandidateFile(root, '/repo/a.css')`. Fixture data cannot cause the fail-open the guard
exists to prevent, so it was a false positive.

**Do not "fix" the flagged file.** The detector is
`ROOT_ISH = /(ROOT|REPO|WORKSPACE|CHECKOUT|TREE_?BASE)/i`, so every rename that keeps the
meaning still trips it, and renaming to something non-root-ish makes the code less clear
purely to satisfy a linter — dodging a detector, not satisfying it. The deciding evidence
was the convention: 7 of the 8 sibling nudge scripts have `selfTest` blocks and none binds
a fixture root. So the **detector** was fixed, not the peer's script.

<Aside type="danger">
End the skipped block on a **column-0 `}`**, never by brace-counting. A brace inside a
string literal miscounts, and the miscount is silent *in the dangerous direction*: an
unbalanced count never re-enables scanning, so the guard quietly stops checking the entire
rest of the file. Pair the change with a control asserting scanning **resumes** after the
block (an offender before *and* after, with the fixture skipped) — that control is the
canary for "it stopped checking."
</Aside>

## The through-line

Every one of these fails toward a confident green. Before trusting a guard, ask what its
green would look like if it were running on nothing — and pick a probe that can tell the
difference. Same family as the documented traps that mining green-checkpoint's
`isolation:` lines returns the gate's **own** test fixtures, and that a `tsc -p .` which
typechecks zero files exits clean.
